brief: Goldman macro sales (Louis Miller) reports clients are rattled less by the 10Y's level than by its speed: about 68bp higher since end-August, closing the week at 5.25% after a 30Y auction priced at 5.618%, the highest since 2000. Front-end hikes are already priced, so selling has shifted to the long end, a bear steepener replacing the earlier bear flattener, driven by real yields (98 of 108bp), which Goldman reads as a cost-of-capital repricing from Treasury and AI-capex funding competing for the same dollar. Oil and rates, which had traded as one asset, have decoupled: bonds fall on bad oil news but no longer rally on good oil news, so clients unable to predict Gulf de-escalation have lost the hedge de-escalation used to provide. The ex-AI S&P, up about 7% versus the index's 14%, has already priced this stress, so Miller would add non-AI exposure into the midterms as a clearing event. The note's own scoreboard shows vol-selling and dispersion topped 2026 strategy returns, meaning record VIX-short and dealer-long-gamma positioning has been paid to assume moves stay small even as rate volatility sits at one-year highs, a mismatch Goldman flags as the real risk, hedged via a VIX call spread.
